facts.text: Toto's had his share of the scraps already. Auntie Em would want me to save some for the Scarecrow.
facts.why: Dorothy never says this. Auntie Em is not in Oz, and the Scarecrow is stuffed with straw and wants a brain, so nobody is saving him food. The one scrap moment is Dorothy tossing a piece of her cruller to Toto on the farm. A real short Dorothy line from that same scene fits the length.
facts.fix: Someplace where there isn't any trouble... do you suppose there is such a place, Toto?

fix_note.text: Someplace where there isn't any trouble... do you suppose there is such a place, Toto?

facts.text: Serve the snacks when Auntie Em hands out the fresh crullers on the farm.
facts.why: In the farm scene Auntie Em tells the hands they cannot work on an empty stomach and offers crullers just fried; Dorothy's own cruller for Toto comes later.

facts.text: Pay no attention to the man behind the curtain.
facts.why: Close nod to the film's line 'Pay no attention to that man behind the curtain!' A plain reference. Not printed in quote marks.

facts.text: The horse of a different colour approves.
facts.why: The Horse of a Different Color in the Emerald City is in the film, and the phrase is the coachman's.

vibe.verdict: Good coverage of the road, the slippers and the monkeys, but the palace banquet is a generic setting and the host note was invented.
